text: The applicant was born in 1979.
The applicant lives in Budapest.
The applicant was represented by Mr D.A. Karsai, a lawyer practising in Budapest.
The Government were represented by their Agent, Mr Z. Tallódi, of the Ministry of Justice.
The facts of the case, as submitted by the parties, may be summarised as follows.
On 11 March 2013, Parliament adopted the Fourth Amendment to the Basic Law of Hungary.
The Fourth Amendment to the Basic Law pertains to numerous, often controversial, issues of fundamental rights.
Under Hungarian law, the President of Hungary had five days to assent to the Fourth Amendment to the Basic Law.
The applicant and other individuals intended to hold a demonstration in front of the President of Hungary's residence.
The purpose of the intended demonstration was to call on the President of Hungary not to assent to the Fourth Amendment to the Basic Law but to refer it to the Constitutional Court.
The applicant informed the Budapest Police Department of his intention to hold a demonstration, in the form of a notification, on 11 March 2013.
On the evening of 11 March 2013, the Budapest Police Department dismissed the applicant's notification without examining it on the merits.
The Budapest Police Department pointed out that the Anti-Terror Centre had closed down the area in front of the President of Hungary's residence from 8 to 16 March 2013.

Because the Anti-Terror Centre had closed down the area in front of the President of Hungary's residence from 8 to 16 March 2013, the Budapest Police Department stated that the area was no longer a public area available for demonstrations during that period.
On 13 March 2013, the President of Hungary announced that he was to assent to the Fourth Amendment to the Basic Law.
On 14 March 2013, the applicant challenged the Budapest Police Department's decision in court.
On 18 March 2013, the Budapest Administrative and Labour Court quashed the Budapest Police Department's decision dismissing the applicant's notification.

The Budapest Administrative and Labour Court held that the Budapest Police Department had failed to provide in its decision the precise reasons why the Anti-Terror Centre had closed down the area in question.

The Budapest Administrative and Labour Court held that the Budapest Police Department had erroneously characterised the applicant's intended demonstration as one outside the scope of the law on peaceful demonstrations.
The applicant submitted that he had subsequently filed an official liability action against the Budapest Police Department.
The Government submitted that on 8 April 2013 the applicant had brought a claim for damages against the Budapest Police Department.
The Government submitted that the applicant's claim for damages against the Budapest Police Department had subsequently been dismissed on 14 May 2013.
